title: Multi-role SaaS boilerplate for a home-services trade, built to sell
summary: A production-ready product for one trade (cleaning, plumbing, HVAC…): owner dashboard, field-worker mobile app, client portal, marketing site, a fictional demo company in the seed, the buyer's kit. From scratch, Next.js + Postgres (PGlite in dev), parallel builders after a frozen foundation.

pitfalls.fix: a reserved port: Deckhand picks bind-tested ports; for your own scripts use `dh dev port`
HOSTNAME from git-bash: Deckhand sets HOSTNAME=127.0.0.1 for servers it starts — start the production build with `dh verify`, not by hand
PGlite takes one connection: pool max 1 in dev

delegate_task: no curly-brace or angle-bracket placeholder in any task text (the whole batch is refused); browser_navigate refuses localhost — builders check pages with curl; each builder uses its own scratch folder
builders never run a production build (it rewrites .next under the dev server) and never restart the dev server
a shell's working directory inside .next/standalone locks it: cd to the project root everywhere, then rebuild
a key pasted in chat: `dh vault set NAME` at once, tell the owner once that it sits in the chat history (rotate it if that history leaves the machine)
